Brent mostly traded around $60–75 through 2025, and forecasts for 2026 pointed to oversupply and soft prices, roughly in the $55–70 range. A close above $85 on August 31, 2026 would likely need a major supply shock, such as a Middle East escalation. Kalshi lists several strikes for each monthly contract, so $84.99 may simply be one of the far-out-of-the-money ones. I don't know the actual August 2026 price, so I'm leaving some room for a geopolitical spike, but the probability is low.

Probability: 0.1

The Dodgers won the 2024 and 2025 titles and were heavy favorites entering 2026, likely the strongest roster in baseball. Even so, the MLB playoffs are close to a coin flip each round, so a top team's title odds rarely exceed about 20–25%. My knowledge ends in June 2026, so I don't know the actual 2026 postseason result. I therefore estimate from strong-favorite base rates.

Probability: 0.22

Katie Hobbs is the Democratic incumbent, and her likely opponent was Andy Biggs, a hard-right Republican. The 2026 midterm under a Republican president should favor Democrats, and Hobbs had a fundraising advantage, though Arizona polling showed a competitive race. The environment date suggests the November election has already happened, but I don't know the result. On balance I lean Democratic.

Probability: 0.64

Polymarket's "Blue tsunami" most likely requires Democrats to win both chambers, probably with a large House margin. I don't know the November 2026 results, since my knowledge stops in June 2026. Winning the House looked fairly likely then, but flipping the Senate needs a net gain of four seats on a tough map, which pre-election markets priced at roughly 35–40%. Adding the likely seat-margin requirement lowers the odds further.

Probability: 0.25

The 2024 measure passed 52–48, and abortion-rights positions have won nearly every post-Dobbs ballot referendum, which makes a repeal an uphill fight. On the other side, the 2026 measure adds popular-sounding provisions (rape/incest exceptions, parental consent, a ban on gender-affirming care for minors), and Missouri's lower-turnout midterm electorate leans Republican. Offsetting that, a 2026 midterm under a Republican president likely favors Democratic-leaning turnout, and the court-rewritten ballot summary reduces any framing advantage. I don't know the actual result, so I put the measure's passage somewhat below even odds.

Probability: 0.4

The 2026 World Series result comes after my June 2026 knowledge cutoff, so I can't confirm the outcome. The Dodgers, two-time defending champions with a deep, expensive roster, were preseason favorites at roughly 20–25% implied odds, and even the best team rarely tops about 30% before the playoffs. You say you're confident it resolves YES, but without a reported result I can only move modestly above the base rate.

Probability: 0.27

Incumbent Democrat Katie Hobbs ran for re-election in 2026, a midterm under a Republican president, which historically favors the out-party. Her likely opponent, Andy Biggs, is a hard-right candidate who may struggle with Arizona's swing electorate. I have no data on the actual result, and Arizona remains very closely divided, so I can't go as far as near-certainty. I estimate Hobbs as a moderate favorite.

Probability: 0.66

I don't know Brent's price in mid-to-late August 2026. Most 2026 forecasts put Brent around $55–70, which would make a close above $85 unlikely. However, Kalshi usually sets strikes near the current price, which suggests Brent was trading close to $85 when this market was listed. Your confidence is noted, but without data I can check, I estimate roughly even odds, shaded slightly below 50% given the lower baseline forecasts.

Probability: 0.45

I can't verify the November 2026 results, so this estimate rests on what was known before the election. A "blue tsunami" market most likely requires Democrats to win both the House and the Senate by large margins. Flipping the Senate on the 2026 map meant a net gain of four seats against a Republican-leaning map, so a sweep with big margins was an upside-tail outcome even in a favorable midterm. Your confidence may reflect results I can't see, so I'm giving a somewhat higher number than the pre-election base rate.

Probability: 0.3

The 2024 amendment passed narrowly, 51.6%, in a presidential year. The 2026 measure is designed to be more appealing: it adds rape and incest exceptions and bundles popular provisions like parental consent and a ban on gender-affirming care for minors. Against that, abortion-rights positions have won nearly every post-Dobbs referendum, a midterm under a Republican president tends to energize Democratic-leaning voters, and court fights over the ballot summary made the repeal more visible. Although the vote has likely happened, I don't know the result, so I put this close to a coin flip with a slight lean toward NO rather than the confident YES you expect.

Probability: 0.45

I don't know the 2026 World Series result, since my knowledge ends in June 2026, so I'm estimating this as if it were still undecided. The Dodgers won the 2024 and 2025 titles and were preseason favorites for 2026 at roughly 20–25%. Even a top playoff team usually wins the World Series only about 15–25% of the time, because short series are close to coin flips. Without information on their final standing or postseason results, and with nothing concrete behind the expectation of a NO, about 18% seems reasonable.

Probability: 0.18

I have no live Brent price data for August 2026, so this relies on prior knowledge: Brent traded mostly around $60–75 through 2025, and futures curves pointed to similar or lower levels for 2026. Reaching above $84.99 would likely require a major supply shock, which I'm not aware of. However, Kalshi usually sets strikes near the prevailing price, so the existence of this strike suggests prices may have been closer to $85 than I'd assume. Weighing that uncertainty, and consistent with your view, I lean toward NO with moderate confidence.

Probability: 0.17
